decided.cycle: dark cells form clusters every ~4.2 weeks that step down one row each time (e.g. ~25, ~55, ~84, ~114, ~143 ... ~291, ~320 ... ~616, ~646), so the spacing is about 29-30 days
decided.week: the rows (weekdays) show no consistent difference in shade; the dark cells drift through every row
decided.level: overall shading of weeks 53-105 looks like that of weeks 1-52
decided.year: a lighter band around weeks ~20-35 shows up again around weeks ~73-90, i.e. at the same time of year
decided.highest_day: the blackest cell is week 88 row 7 (day 616), but week 42 row 4 and week 93 row 2 are nearly as dark, so I am not sure
decided.second_day: week 42 row 4 (day 291) is black; day 646 is a close alternative
decided.peak_shape: the cells next to the darkest ones are also dark-gray, so each peak lasts 2-3 days
decided.drops: no near-white cells stand alone; the light cells are in broad seasonal bands
decided.stands_out: only the blackest cells inside the recurring dark clusters; the clusters themselves are periodic, not singular

answer.guess: Something tied to the lunar (~29.5-day) cycle, e.g. searches or visits related to the full moon or to menstrual cycles, with a summer dip.
